newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up as political worries ease.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up as political worries ease.

text.p: Taiwan share prices continued to rebound on Tuesday as political worries eased on reports that President Lee Teng-hui would meet provincial governor James Soong, who has tendered his resignation, brokers said.
Soong, a ruling Nationalist Party heavyweight, has refused to back Lee's plan to dismantle his provincial administration.
His resignation followed an all-party decision in December to freeze provincial-level elections as a first step in the process, which Taipei says would end redundancy in government.
The index ended up 30.27 points or 0.44 percent to 6,875.02, off a 6,897.39 high. Turnover was an active T$50.61 billion.
The market plunged 1.64 percent on Saturday as investors worried that Soong's resignation would cause instability.
"It seems the impact of Soong's resignation has come to an end, especially after reports that President Lee will meet Soong to seek solutions," said Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang.
The second rebound in as many days was fuelled by the entry of government-related fund to support the market in the face of the political uncertainty, brokers said.
But buying continued cautious ahead of Thursday's launch of Taiwan stock index futures by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and Singapore International Monetary Exchange, they said.
"Investors still don't know what the real impact of the CME and SIMEX moves on the spot market will be," Huang said.
In the meantime, some investors have gravitated toward the young over-the-counter stock market, she said.

Finance Minister Paul Chiu, remaining noncommittal on the offshore futures, said on Tuesday that Taiwan regarded the CME and SIMEX contracts as positive but declined to endorse them or lift rules that forbids Taiwan investors to trade them.
Electronics led Tuesday's gains, rising 2.05 percent. First International Computer rose up T$2 to T$54.
